title: Disclosure, Confidentiality and Insider Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors, Officers, Employees and Representatives
tiers.description: Any director, officer or employee of the Company, plus any consultant or contractor (Representative) who receives Company information or is authorized to speak on its behalf. Subject only to the general ban on dealing while in possession of Undisclosed Material Information.

tiers.name: Individuals who participate in the preparation of the Company's financial statements or who are privy to material financial information relating to the Company, including the Board
tiers.description: Additionally prohibited from purchasing or selling Company securities during the quarterly/annual blackout period, and any other period designated by the Disclosure Committee.

applies_to: Individuals who participate in the preparation of the Company's financial statements or who are privy to material financial information relating to the Company, including the Board
windows.start_anchor: tenth Trading Day prior to the planned release date of Company's quarterly or annual financial results
windows.end_anchor: first full Trading Day after the financial results for a fiscal quarter or fiscal year end have been filed on SEDAR

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Disclosure Committee may designate any other period during which directors, officers, employees and Representatives 'so advised' are prohibited from purchasing or selling securities. Confidentiality of the reason is not addressed.

rules.detail: No definition of 'securities' extends to derivatives, and no provision mentions options, swaps, forwards, puts or calls in relation to personal dealing; the only 'securities' referenced are the Company's own shares and its employee stock options/RSUs.
Hedging is never mentioned and there is no concept of 'limiting economic risk' anywhere in the Policy.

Monetisation is named expressly, but the only trigger for the ban is possession of Undisclosed Material Information; it is not banned generally, is not subject to any clearance or pre-approval requirement, and is not tied to vesting status.
rules.evidence: No person shall purchase or sell or otherwise monetize securities of the Company while in possession of Undisclosed Material Information.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

Margin lending against personal shareholdings is not mentioned; Schedule A's reference to 'borrowing or lending of a significant amount of money' concerns the Company's own capital structure as an item of material information, not personal margin loans.

Personal pledges, charges or liens over securities are not mentioned; Schedule A's 'mortgaging or encumbering of the company's assets' concerns the Company's own assets as a materiality example, not a personal encumbrance rule.
There is no provision addressing secured financing, margin accounts or forced sales in respect of personally held Company securities.
No minimum holding period, intention test or short-swing rule is imposed; the only timing restriction is the quarterly blackout window, which is a closed period rather than a short-term dealing rule.

clearance.tier: Individuals who participate in the preparation of the Company's financial statements or who are privy to material financial information relating to the Company, including the Board
clearance.evidence: an individual may purchase or sell securities during any blackout period with the prior written consent of the Chief Executive Officer. The Chief Executive Officer may grant permission to purchase or sell during a blackout period only in the case of unusual, exceptional circumstances.

exceptions.evidence: Unusual, exceptional circumstances may include the sale of securities in the case of severe financial hardship or where the timing of the sale is critical for significant tax planning purposes.

the above prohibition excludes the exercise or redemption of any stock option, restricted share unit or similar security however it includes the sale of those securities acquired though the exercise or redemption.

exemption_authority: The Chief Executive Officer may grant prior written consent to purchase or sell during a blackout period only in unusual, exceptional circumstances (e.g. severe financial hardship or critical tax planning). No other exemption or waiver authority is described, and there is no general pre-clearance system for dealing outside a blackout period.
jurisdiction_overlays: Canadian securities law (Securities Act (British Columbia)) and BCSC/SEDAR filing regime
Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX) listing rules and IIROC pre-clearance of press releases issued during trading hours

bespoke_clauses.clause: No person shall purchase or sell or otherwise monetize securities of the Company while in possession of Undisclosed Material Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only clause that plainly reaches an OTC collar (naming 'monetize'), but it only bars entry while the individual holds undisclosed material information; the separate quarterly blackout provision is worded narrower ('purchasing or selling') and does not on its face use the word 'monetize', creating a textual gap for collar entry during the blackout window if no MNPI is held.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy imposes no requirement to seek clearance or give notice before dealing, other than the Chief Executive Officer's written consent needed to deal during a blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside the quarterly blackout and while free of undisclosed material information, a director or executive can enter, unwind or roll a collar without company approval, which simplifies timing but leaves the bank with no company sign-off trail confirming the trade is compliant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy covers all written or oral communications and applies to any director, officer or employee of the Company. It also applies to any consultant or contractor (a 'Representative').
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Spouses, trusts and controlled entities are not mentioned, so routing the collar or its security through a related vehicle is not addressed or restricted by the document.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Company complies with its timely disclosure obligations as required under applicable Canadian securities laws, including the Securities Act (British Columbia)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy is drafted for a TSX-listed, BCSC-regulated issuer with no reference to ASX Listing Rules or the Australian insider trading regime, so an Australian bank should confirm which regime actually governs the executive's holding before relying on this document alone.

bespoke_clauses.topic: silence on secured financing and derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: (No provision addresses margin loans, pledges, encumbrances, derivatives, hedging, short selling, stock lending or CFDs.)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: None of the structural elements of a funded collar (the put, the call, or the loan secured on the shares) is expressly prohibited, permitted or made subject to clearance, so the transaction is not blocked by the Policy but also receives no express safe harbour.

summary: This Policy is a disclosure and insider trading policy, not a comprehensive securities dealing policy, and it is silent on derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance, secured financing, short selling, stock lending, CFDs and short-term dealing. A funded collar is therefore not expressly prohibited, but the only operative restrictions are: (i) no director, officer, employee or Representative may purchase, sell or 'otherwise monetize' Company securities while in possession of Undisclosed Material Information; and (ii) individuals privy to material financial information (including the Board) may not purchase or sell during the ten-trading-day pre-results blackout (extending to first full trading day after filing) without the Chief Executive Officer's prior written consent, granted only for hardship or tax-timing reasons. There is no pre-clearance system for ordinary dealing outside the blackout, no minimum shareholding requirement, and no restriction tied to vesting status. A funded collar over vested shares could proceed provided the executive holds no undisclosed material information at signing, is outside any applicable blackout (or obtains CEO consent), and the transaction and its governing law are confirmed against the Company's actual Canadian/TSX regulatory obligations rather than assumed ASX norms.
